conn.p1: The app runs locally on both computers, but it may use the internet. That is how your two apps find each other – no server of your own, no account, no router settings:
conn.p1Group: The app runs locally on every computer, but it may use the internet. That is how your apps find each other – no server of your own, no account, no router settings:
conn.p2: Both apps announce themselves with your room code on public Nostr relays. The relays only introduce you – after that your apps talk directly (WebRTC, like a video call).
conn.p2Group: All apps announce themselves with your room code on public Nostr relays. The relays only introduce you – after that your apps talk directly (WebRTC, like a video call).
conn.p3: If a router blocks direct connections, data goes through a public MQTT server instead. It also keeps your latest state, so the others catch up even if you are not online at the same time.
conn.p4: Everything is encrypted with the key from your invite. Only tracker data travels – never ROMs or save files.

faq.a2a: It reads your game live – team, HP, levels, catches – but it never writes into the running game. That keeps your save safe.
faq.a2b: Between sessions it can edit your save file: dead Pokémon can be moved into PC box 18 (graveyard). This only works while the game is closed, and a backup is made first.
faq.a3: No. Everyone uses their own copy. The invite only contains settings, seeds and the room key; the randomizer rebuilds the identical game from your own ROM, and the app checks the checksum.
faq.a4: All main Pokémon games on Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS (Gen 1–5) and their ROM hacks, plus X/Y to Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon on Nintendo 3DS (Gen 6–7). Live tracking works for the English and German releases; ROM hacks work when they keep the original memory layout.
faq.a5: Yes – choose them in the settings. mGBA streams live data through a small script you load once (Tools › Scripting). melonDS has no scripting, so it syncs after every in-game save.
faq.a6: Nothing gets lost. Each app keeps its own copy and both merge automatically when you’re connected again.
faq.a7: Right after it happens, save the diagnostics and send the file along with what you did. It holds what souldew read from the game and decided this session (song numbers, levels, what the turbo sound played) – no ROM, save file or invite.
faq.a8a: No analytics, and an account only if you want one. By itself souldew sends an anonymous “playing now” heartbeat for the player count on the souldew Discord: while a game runs, once a minute, the system (GB, GBA, DS, 3DS), the mode (solo, Nuzlocke, SoulLink or Play together), the app version and a random id that is new for every game. No name, no game title, no run, no ROM – and the IP address isn’t stored. Besides that it only checks for updates. Signed in with a souldew account, your friends see that you’re online and what you play – Settings › Account › Privacy decides how much, and “Appear offline” shares none of it.
faq.a8b: Don’t want to be counted? Switch off “Count me in ‘playing now’” in Settings › Online – it stops right away.
faq.a9a: Yes. In the library, open the game › “Import a save file …” (in a run: the board’s Files menu). It takes .sav, .srm and DeSmuME’s .dsv from other emulators, flash carts and cartridge dumps, checks the size and – for the Pokémon games – whether it is a save of that game, and backs up the save it replaces first, with Undo.
faq.a9b: “Save game file” gives you a plain .sav that other emulators and flash carts read. In a run, an imported save is logged for everyone, a SoulLink needs the host to allow it, and what it brings along doesn’t count for the run or your trophies. 3DS: a Checkpoint or JKSM backup goes into souldew’s own 3DS player once the game has saved there.

guide.s1: Library › Add files. ROMs (.gb, .gbc, .gba, .nds, .zip) and ROM-hack patches are copied into your library.
guide.s2Nav: SoulLink › Host new SoulLink: pick a game (and optionally a hack), the number of players, a randomizer preset and the names. The app builds the games in seconds.
guide.s3Nav: Create a code for each player (or send the invite file). Everyone adds their own copy of the game and gets an identical game – no ROM ever has to be shared. Playing alone? Use Nuzlocke › New Nuzlocke instead and skip this step.
guide.s4Nav: Press “Play” on the board or “Continue” in the overview. Your team, levels and HP are read live and appear on everyone’s board within a second. The game keeps running in the corner while you look elsewhere – the green light in the sidebar shows where it belongs.
guide.s5: If a linked Pokémon faints, the pair dies for both of you automatically. The board, the graveyard and the log keep the score.

rnd.additionalImportantTrainerPokemon: Extra Pokémon for rival / villain team
rnd.assignEvoStatsRandomly: Spread the stats gained on evolution randomly
rnd.balanceShakingGrass.help: Shaking grass gets Pokémon of a fitting strength.
rnd.banRegularShopItems: No regular shop items (Potions, Poké Balls …)
rnd.baseStatsFollowMegaEvolutions: Mega Evolutions keep the stat spread
rnd.changeImpossibleEvolutions.help: Important without a trading partner – some ROM hacks already do this themselves.
rnd.eliteFourUniquePokemonNumber.help: Their strongest Pokémon appear on no other trainer.
rnd.fullHMCompat: Every Pokémon can learn every HM
rnd.fullHMCompat.help: Handy when the randomizer leaves you without HM users.
rnd.highestLevelOnlyGetsItemsForTrainerP: Only the highest-level Pokémon gets an item
rnd.limitMainGameLegendaries.help: Legendaries you must face in the story (e.g. Lugia / Ho-Oh) get a beatable replacement.
rnd.moveTutorMovesMod.help: Only games with move tutors – ignored otherwise.
rnd.preset.chaos.description: Almost everything random: types, abilities, evolutions, movesets, TMs, items. Only for the brave.
rnd.preset.chaos.name: Chaos
rnd.preset.hardcore.description: Like classic + trainers, but tougher: +20 % trainer levels, extra Pokémon for bosses and rivals, sensible held items, smarter movesets.
rnd.preset.hardcore.name: Nuzlocke hard mode
rnd.preset.light.description: Only wild Pokémon are random; everything else stays as in the original game.
rnd.preset.light.name: Wild only
rnd.preset.soullink-trainers.description: Like classic, plus random trainer teams of similar strength (rival keeps their starter, bosses get +1 Pokémon).
rnd.preset.soullink-trainers.name: Classic + trainers
rnd.preset.soullink.description: Random wild Pokémon & starters (similar strength); trainers keep their original teams. Fair, exciting, no broken movesets.
rnd.preset.soullink.name: Classic
rnd.preset.vanilla-plus.description: The original Pokémon everywhere, with quality-of-life fixes: no trade evolutions, better catch rates, moves and stats as in newer games, faster text.
rnd.preset.vanilla-plus.name: Vanilla+
rnd.randomizeWildPokemonHeldItems: Randomize items held by wild Pokémon
rnd.sensibleItemsOnlyForTrainerPokemon.h: Items that fit the Pokémon (e.g. a Yache Berry only on Ice-weak Pokémon).
rnd.shopItemsMod.help: Only the special shops change: department store floors, herb and vitamin sellers and the second counter of a Poké Mart. The regular Poké Mart items stay – in FireRed/LeafGreen just Celadon Department Store 4F and 5F change. No shops in Gen 1/2.
rnd.startersMod.help: With two evolutions: basic Pokémon that evolve twice – fair and never legendary.
rnd.staticPokemonMod.help: Not possible for ROM hacks that move the event scripts – it is set to "Unchanged" automatically there.
rnd.swapStaticMegaEvos.help: A gift Pokémon that can Mega Evolve (e.g. Lucario) becomes another one that can.
rnd.swapTrainerMegaEvos.help: A trainer whose Pokémon Mega Evolves gets another Pokémon that can.
rnd.tmLevelUpMoveSanity: Pokémon can learn TMs of their level-up moves
rnd.tmsFollowMoves: TM compatibility follows the new TM moves
rnd.tmsFollowMoves.help: A TM with a new move works for the Pokémon that could learn that move in the original game – by TM, tutor or level-up, also as an earlier evolution. A move no Pokémon could learn goes to the Pokémon of its type. HMs stay as they are.
rnd.totemPokemonMod.help: The bosses at the end of the island trials.
rnd.trainersMatchTypingDistribution: Weight types by how many Pokémon have them
rnd.trainersMatchTypingDistribution.help: Fewer repeats, but sometimes several trainers of one type in a row.
rnd.trainersMod.TYPE_THEMED_ELITE4_GYMS: Type theme for gyms & Elite Four only
rnd.trainersMod.help: "Unchanged" keeps the trainers' original teams – including the reworked teams of ROM hacks.
rnd.tutorLevelUpMoveSanity: Pokémon can learn tutor moves of their level-up moves
rnd.tweak.NATIONAL_DEX_AT_START: National Pokédex from the start (needed so Pokémon from other regions can evolve)
rnd.tweak.RANDOMIZE_PC_POTION: Randomize the Potion in your PC
rnd.tweak.SOS_BATTLES_FOR_ALL: All wild Pokémon can call allies
rnd.updateBaseStats: Update base stats to a newer generation
rnd.updateMoves: Update moves to a newer generation
rnd.updateMoves.help: Power, accuracy and PP as in later games (no new Fairy type).
rnd.useTimeBasedEncounters.help: Morning, day and night get their own pools.
rnd.weighDuplicateAbilitiesTogether.help: E.g. Insomnia and Vital Spirit share one chance.
rnd.wildPokemonMod.help: Recommended for SoulLinks: completely random – the most variety per route.
rnd.wildPokemonRestrictionMod.CATCH_EM_A: Catch 'em all (every Pokémon at least once)

rules.autoAssignHint: Based on where they were caught. Unclear cases land in the inbox.
rules.autoDeath: A linked Pokémon that faints (live) kills the pair automatically
rules.autoDeathGroup: A linked Pokémon that faints (live) kills its whole group automatically
rules.b1: Only the first Pokémon you meet in each area counts. Both catches of an area form a pair.
rules.b1Group: Only the first Pokémon you meet in each area counts. All players’ catches on an area are linked into a group.
rules.b1Solo: Only the first Pokémon you meet in each area may be caught. If it flees or faints, the area is used up.
rules.b2: If one Pokémon faints, its partner dies too – both go to the graveyard.
rules.b2Group: If one Pokémon faints, every Pokémon linked to it dies too – the whole group goes to the graveyard.
rules.b2Solo: A Pokémon that faints is dead – it goes to the graveyard and is never used again.
rules.b3: A pair is always in the team together or in the box together.
rules.b3Group: A group is always in the team together or in the box together.
rules.b4: If one of you blacks out, the run is over for both.
rules.b4Group: If one of you blacks out, the run is over for everyone.
rules.b4Solo: If your whole team faints (blackout), the run is over.
rules.b4SoloBox: The run is over once no living Pokémon is left – in the team or in the box.
rules.b4SoloOff: A blackout doesn’t end the run – you decide when it’s over.
rules.balls: Nothing counts before your first Poké Balls
rules.ballsHint: Each of you starts with your own first Poké Balls: until then your Pokémon don’t die, a blackout doesn’t end the run and no area is used up. When your partner’s rules have started and they lose a Pokémon, yours still dies with it. Both of you need souldew 2.8.3 or newer.
rules.ballsHintGroup: Each of you starts with your own first Poké Balls: until then your Pokémon don’t die, a blackout doesn’t end the run and no area is used up. When someone whose rules have started loses a Pokémon, the linked ones still die with it. Everyone needs souldew 2.8.3 or newer.
rules.ballsHintSolo: Until you have Poké Balls in your bag, a Pokémon that faints doesn’t die, a blackout doesn’t end the run and no area is used up – reset or play on. The rules start the moment souldew sees your first Poké Balls (or your first catch).
rules.ballsWaitingMine: You: waiting for your first Poké Balls – your own Pokémon don’t die yet.
rules.ballsWaitingOther: {name}: waiting for the first Poké Balls.
rules.ballsWaitingSolo: Waiting for your first Poké Balls – nothing counts yet.
rules.capsHint: Warns when a Pokémon is above the next boss’s ace level.
rules.cheatSetOld: A partner on souldew 2.x can’t see this choice: their app offers its own cheats (Rare Candies) whenever cheats are on – each use still shows up in the log.
rules.cheatsHintAll: From the play screen’s cheats menu: items into the bag and money – pick which ones. Every use shows up in the log for both of you.
rules.cheatsHintGroupAll: From the play screen’s cheats menu: items into the bag and money – pick which ones. Every use shows up in the log for all of you.
rules.discordHint: Optional: post catches and deaths to your Discord channel (Channel › Integrations › Webhook).
rules.discordLocal: Stays on this computer – your partner can add their own.
rules.discordLocalGroup: Stays on this computer – the others can add their own.
rules.dupesAllHint: For everyone: a line one of you caught doesn’t count again for any of you.
rules.dupesBothHint: For both: a line one of you caught doesn’t count again for either of you.
rules.dupesHint: Already own the evolution line? Keep looking.
rules.dupesOffHint: Off: every first encounter counts, even one of a line you already caught.
rules.dupesPlayerHint: Per player: a line you caught yourself doesn’t count again for you – the others’ catches don’t matter for you.
rules.dupesWhich: Every catch counts, also one whose pair failed or died – a Pokémon that fled or was knocked out doesn’t.
rules.dupesWhichGroup: Every catch counts, also one whose group failed or died – a Pokémon that fled or was knocked out doesn’t.
rules.dupesWhichGroupMissed: Every catch counts, also one whose group failed or died.
rules.dupesWhichMissed: Every catch counts, also one whose pair failed or died.
rules.fail: A missed encounter costs the whole pair
rules.failGroup: A missed encounter costs the whole group
rules.failHint: Fled or knocked out: your partner’s Pokémon from that area may not be used either.
rules.failHintGroup: Fled or knocked out: the others’ Pokémon from that area may not be used either.
rules.giftsHint: Starter aside: eggs, trades, fossils and gift Pokémon. A free extra stays out of the pairs, like a bonus shiny.
rules.giftsHintGroup: Starter aside: eggs, trades, fossils and gift Pokémon. A free extra stays out of the groups, like a bonus shiny.
rules.hostOnly: Only the host can change this.
rules.itemGiftsHint: Give each other items from your bags – walk up and press A, or from the board. Never key items, TMs or the Master Ball. Off for a stricter run.
rules.linkBattleDeaths: Losing a link battle counts as deaths
rules.linkBattleDeathsHint: Off: a link battle is just for fun – Pokémon that go down there are fine afterwards.
rules.linkBattlesHint2: A link battle in the Colosseum or the Union Room.
rules.linkTradesHint: The real in-game trade in the Pokémon Center – a traded Pokémon keeps its link.
rules.linkTradesHintCasual: The real in-game trade in the Pokémon Center.
rules.linkWagersHint: The challenger may put in-game money on a battle – the loser’s game pays the winner’s. Money only, never Pokémon or items.
rules.missedDupes: Fled or knocked-out encounters count as dupes
rules.missedDupesHint: Like a catch, once it’s known which Pokémon it was – souldew notes it when it sees the battle.
rules.notHostHere: Only the computer that created this run can change its rules.
rules.raidDeathsHint: A raid is a real battle. Off: Pokémon that go down in it don’t count – heal them at a Pokémon Center.
rules.raidsHint: Fight the next trainer together: every hit in anybody’s game comes off one shared HP pool, so it’s beaten in everyone’s game at once.
rules.saveImportsHint: For a lost or old save: load a .sav into your game. It shows up in the log for both of you, and what the save brings along doesn’t count – no catches, badges or trophies from it.
rules.saveImportsHintGroup: For a lost or old save: load a .sav into your game. It shows up in the log for all of you, and what the save brings along doesn’t count – no catches, badges or trophies from it.
rules.setByHostText: {name} created this run and sets the rules for everyone – only {name} can change them. Every change shows up in the log.
rules.shiny: Shiny clause: shinies may always be caught and stay unlinked
rules.sumBalls: Nothing counts before the first Poké Balls
rules.typeHelpHint: In battle: how your moves land, what hits you and each Pokémon’s weaknesses. Off hides it for every player.
rules.typeHelpHintSolo: In battle: how your moves land, what hits you and each Pokémon’s weaknesses. Off for a run where you work them out yourself.
rules.typeHint: Primary types may not repeat in the team.
rules.youHost: You’re the host: your rules apply to both of you. Every change you make shows up in the log for both of you.
rules.youHostGroup: You’re the host: your rules apply to all of you. Every change you make shows up in the log for everyone.
runs.deleteText: This removes the run from this computer: the games built for it, the save files, the board with all encounters and deaths, and the invite.
runs.deleteTrash: The folder is moved to the trash folder inside the app data (runs/.trash) – you can restore it by hand. Your partner’s copy is not affected.
runs.deleteTrashGroup: The folder is moved to the trash folder inside the app data (runs/.trash) – you can restore it by hand. The copies of the other players are not affected.
runs.deleteTrashSolo: The folder is moved to the trash folder inside the app data (runs/.trash) – you can restore it by hand.

set.backupFailed: souldew couldn’t make a backup before 3.0. Your data is as it was.
set.backupHint: The folder “{name}” is in the “backups” folder inside souldew’s data folder. souldew never touches it again – delete it once you’re sure you don’t need it.
set.backupMade: Before its first start, souldew 3.0 backed up your runs, saves, save states, settings and trophies ({size}, {date}) – not your games, which stay where they are.
set.backupNoSpace: souldew didn’t make a backup before 3.0: the disk had {free} free, the backup needs {need} and leaves room for your games. Your data is as it was – nothing was changed for lack of space.
set.coffeePop: Coffee hint on legendary encounters in stream overlays
set.coffeePopHint: Now and then a cheeky toast about the legendary pops up in your Alerts overlay, with the coffee link.
set.connElsewhere: Invite codes, relays and who is online:
set.controlsText2: Keyboard keys for the built-in emulator and its shortcuts. Click a key, then press the new one – any key can go to any button or shortcut, and shortcuts can also be switched off. Changes apply right away, also to a game that is running.
set.ctrFfHint: Tell me when it slows down fast-forward
set.ctrFfHintHint: On some graphics cards fast-forward at 2× or 3× stays well below the speed you pick – the play view then says so, at most once each time souldew starts.
set.ctrRendererHint: How souldew’s built-in 3DS player draws the game. Automatic starts with Vulkan; if the game stops right after starting, it switches to Vulkan (compatibility) and then to Software, and remembers that for this graphics card and driver. Software works on every PC but is much slower. Applies to the next 3DS game you start.
set.ctrRendererLearned: This graphics card currently plays 3DS games with: {mode}
set.ctrScaleHint: Draws the 3DS games at two or three times their own resolution – sharper and less pixelated, but more work for the graphics card. Applies to the next 3DS game you start. The Software renderer always plays at 1×, and so does the automatic step down after a crash.
set.emptyText: Try a shorter word – for example turbo, controller, language or Discord.
set.emuText: The built-in emulator plays every system up to the Nintendo 3DS and has the best live sync. 3DS games can also run in Azahar (for example when a graphics card can’t run the built-in 3DS player). External emulators are optional otherwise.
set.engineHint: The fast player on souldew’s own engine: one player for DS, GBA and Game Boy that trades and battles straight from your running game – your partners join it, nobody’s game restarts. Same speed, save states, cheats and live sync as the fast player. Off: the fast player as before. Applies to the next game you start.
set.fullTurbo: Full-power turbo: no brake while fast-forwarding
set.fullTurboHint: The game may use almost all of the computer’s time while fast-forwarding, and DS games skip drawing frames nobody sees. Never steps down. If the app reacts sluggishly while fast-forwarding, turn it off. Normal speed stays the same.
set.gbLookHint: Red, Blue, Yellow and the other Game Boy games in the fast player: on the original Game Boy with its green screen, or with the colours a Game Boy Color gives them. Gold, Silver and Crystal are always in colour. Applies to the next game you start; a savestate loads only with the look it was made with.
set.gpuFallbackCrash: The graphics backend {backend} kept crashing. souldew uses “Automatic” again from the next start – you can change it in Settings.
set.gpuFallbackStart: souldew didn’t open with the graphics backend {backend}, so it uses “Automatic” again. You can change it in Settings.
set.gpuHint: If the game stutters or the sound crackles, try Vulkan. Automatic lets the system decide.
set.gpuRestart: The new graphics backend is used after a restart of souldew.
set.gpuSafeNote: souldew runs in safe graphics mode (software rendering, slower). If the window stays blank in a normal start, pick another graphics backend here – Vulkan or OpenGL often help – then restart normally.
set.gpuSafeToast: souldew draws without the graphics card this time (slower). Pick another graphics backend in Settings › About › Troubleshooting, then restart normally.
set.gpuSafeToastMac: souldew draws without the graphics card this time (slower). Quit and start it again for the normal mode.
set.legal: Pokémon and all related names are trademarks of Nintendo, Game Freak and The Pokémon Company. souldew is a fan project and does not include or download games.
set.libraryText: Games you add are copied into the library folder. You can also include folders where your ROMs already are.
set.mgbaScriptAgain: For live data with mGBA: Tools › Scripting… › File › Load script… and pick this file (again after every mGBA restart):
set.nag: Show the joke license window now and then
set.nagHint: A parody of old shareware nag screens. souldew stays free either way.
set.name: Your name
set.native: Fast player for DS, GBA and Game Boy
set.nativeHint: Runs the game with the real emulators (melonDS, mGBA, SameBoy) directly on your computer: full speed even on weaker PCs, and fast-forward that really reaches 4× and more. Live sync, cheats, save states and the in-game save work as before. Save states from the other player can’t be loaded here (and the other way round). Off: the browser emulator as before. Applies to the next game you start.
set.presenceHint: Only while a game runs: system, mode (solo, Nuzlocke, SoulLink or Play together) and app version with a random id, for the player count on the souldew Discord – no name, no game, no IP stored.
set.shareScreenAll: Share my screen with the other players
set.shareScreenHint: While you play, the others see your game small in a corner. It is only sent while someone is watching.
set.soundsAll: Sounds on this computer (start-up chime, catches, deaths, badges, pings)
set.speedGuard: Step down when the computer can’t keep up
set.speedGuardHint: Off: the speed you pick stays as it is, the bar shows when a scene runs slower. On: a level that isn’t reached for a few seconds drops to the highest one that holds.
set.speedNote: How fast-forward behaves. The speed itself is picked in the game’s bar.
set.streamElsewhere: Streamer mode, OBS overlays and their links:
set.themeText: Colour scheme of the whole app. The colour-blind schemes replace the green/red signals (alive, dead, warnings) with colours that stay apart with that colour vision.
set.troubleNote: Only needed when something doesn’t work – the defaults are right for most computers.
set.turboMax: Turbo step “Max”: as fast as this computer can
set.turboMaxHint: After 4× comes “Max” – no speed limit at all. How fast it gets depends on the game and the computer.
set.uiScaleBrowser: In the browser, its own zoom sizes souldew: {bigger} and {smaller}.
set.uiScaleFit: This window has room for {size} – make it larger and it grows to {chosen}.
set.uiScaleGame: While a game fills the window, these keys stay its shortcuts: {list} (Settings › Controls).
set.uiScaleHint: How big souldew draws its menus, panels, the board and text on this computer – for big, sharp screens. The game itself isn’t scaled: it keeps filling the room it has, pixel-sharp. {bigger}, {smaller} and {reset} change it anywhere.
set.volumeElsewhere: Game volume and mute are in the game’s sound menu (M mutes).
set.wholePixelsHint: Every game pixel exactly 2, 3, 4 … screen pixels big – the crispest picture, with a slim black border when the game doesn’t fill the space exactly. Only when that costs at most about 15 % of the picture; otherwise, and with this off, the picture fills the space with sharp pixels that are smoothed only at their edges.
simp.backup: Your current save{when} is backed up first – Undo brings it back.
simp.copyHint: Your current save as a plain .sav – other emulators and flash carts read it.
simp.ctrStart: Start this game in souldew once and save in it first – then its save can be replaced.
simp.doneBackup: Your old save is backed up. Start the game to go on from the imported one.
simp.doneNew: Start the game to go on from it.
simp.emuOpen: An emulator is still open. Save in the game, close the emulator, then come back.
simp.hostOnly: The host hasn’t allowed importing saves in this run. They can switch it on in the run’s rules.
simp.intro: A save from another emulator, a flash cart or a cartridge dump (.sav, .srm, .dsv …) replaces the save of {game}.
simp.intro3ds: A backup from Checkpoint or JKSM – the folder, or a zip of it – goes into this game’s save in souldew’s own 3DS player.
simp.introRun: A save from another emulator, a flash cart or a cartridge dump (.sav, .srm, .dsv …) replaces your save in the run “{run}”.
simp.match: A save of {game} – it fits this game.
simp.mismatch: This looks like a save of {found}, not of {want}. The game may not load it – or start a new game over it.
simp.missing3ds: Files the game has now that the backup doesn’t: {list} – they are removed.
simp.n.clockDropped: The clock data at its end is left out – this game has no clock.
simp.n.clockKept: The cartridge clock in it comes along.
simp.n.clockWidened: Its clock is in the older VBA-M layout – brought into the current one.
simp.n.dsv: A DeSmuME save (.dsv): its footer is taken off – the save itself stays as it is.

stream.dragHint: Drag into OBS: it becomes a browser source of the right size
stream.followOff: These links always show “{name}”, even when you play another run. Pick “Current run” for links that keep working from run to run.
stream.followOn: The links follow the run you play: start a new run or open another one and the overlays switch by themselves – OBS keeps the same sources. Now: {name}
stream.inObsHint: An overlay with this widget is open outside the app – in OBS or a browser.
stream.modeOff: Switch it on before you go live – souldew then covers what your viewers mustn’t see.
stream.modeOn: souldew is safe to show: everything below is covered on every page until you switch it off.
stream.noRunText: The overlays show a run live. Start a SoulLink or a Nuzlocke first.
stream.obsCount: one overlay live in OBS|{count} overlays live in OBS
stream.onAirHint: Streamer mode is on – codes, keys, paths and spoilers are covered
stream.plBusy: Port {port} is taken – is Pokélink itself open? Close it or pick another port.
stream.plLocal: Also themes from another web server on this computer (localhost, any port) – themes opened from disk or from Pokélink’s website work without it
stream.plNote: Instead of the name, user=p1 … p8 works too. Themes show what Pokélink’s data has: team, levels, HP, status, items, moves and badges.
stream.plOffHint: Off – nothing listens until you switch it on.
stream.plText: Already have a Pokélink theme you like? souldew can feed it: switch the bridge on, then open the theme with one of the endings below instead of its own ?user=… – in OBS just like before.
stream.s1: Pick a widget and set it up – the preview is exactly what OBS shows, live.
stream.s2: Drag “Drag into OBS” onto your scene – OBS makes a browser source of the right size. Or copy the URL into a new browser source.
stream.s3: Keep souldew open while you stream: the overlays update the moment something happens.
stream.testNoObs: It shows in the preview. No alert overlay is open in OBS yet – add the Alerts widget there.
stream.testObs: It shows in the preview and in one overlay outside the app.|It shows in the preview and in {count} overlays outside the app.
stream.wAlertsText: Deaths, catches, badges, evolutions and every 10th level pop up for a few seconds – with sound if you like.
stream.wCardText: One player’s team in detail: nicknames, levels, HP, status, badges and play time.
stream.wCountersText: Alive, in the graveyard, caught and badges – the numbers pop when they change.
stream.wStatsText: Run name, play time, badges and the counts in one slim line – for the bottom of the screen.
stream.wTeamText: Every team side by side – one column per linked group, with level, HP and status. Dead groups turn grey.
stream.wWhereText: The route or town each player is in right now, and the battle they are fighting.

upd.availableSide: Version {version} is available – see the sidebar.
upd.badSignature: The update could not be verified: its signature is missing or wrong, so it was not downloaded. Your installed version is unchanged.
upd.browser: Updates are installed by the desktop app.
upd.dataSafe: Your runs, saves and settings are kept: they live in your Library folder, not inside the app.
upd.dataSafeLinux: Your runs, saves and settings are kept: they live in ~/.config/SoulLink Studio, not inside the app.
upd.dataSafeWin: Your runs, saves and settings are kept: they live in your user folder (AppData), not inside the app.
upd.errChecksum: The download is damaged or was changed – try again.
upd.errCodeSignature: The new version’s code signature doesn’t verify, so it wasn’t installed.
upd.errDmg: The disk image doesn’t contain the expected version of souldew.
upd.errFeed: The update information from the server isn’t valid.
upd.errHttp: The update server answered with an error – try again later.
upd.errInsecure: The update server pointed to an insecure address, so the update was stopped.
upd.errNoAsset: This update has no download for this computer.
upd.errNoKey: This build can’t verify updates, so it doesn’t install any.
upd.errNoStaged: The downloaded update is missing – download it again.
upd.errSameVersion: This update isn’t newer than the installed version.
upd.errSignatureFeed: The update could not be verified: its signature is missing or wrong, so it wasn’t installed.
upd.errTimeout: The update server didn’t answer in time – check the internet connection and try again.

upd.laterHint: The update is installed when you quit the app.
upd.manual2: In the Finder window that opened, drag souldew onto Applications and choose “Replace”.
upd.manual2Linux: In the folder that opened is {file}, already executable. Replace your old souldew AppImage with it – under the old file name if a Steam or desktop shortcut points to it.
upd.manual2Win: In the Explorer window that opened, double-click {file}. It installs the new version and keeps your data.
upd.manualText: Version {version} is downloaded and checked. Replace the app by hand to finish.
upd.manualTextWin: Version {version} is downloaded and checked. Run the installer to finish.
upd.noRelease: No update has been published yet.
upd.notConfigured: Updates are not set up for this build.
upd.readyText: Restart to use version {version}. Your runs, saves and settings stay as they are.
upd.readyTextWin: Restart to install version {version} – it takes a few seconds, then souldew opens again. Your runs, saves and settings stay as they are.
upd.reasonBlocked: macOS did not let the app replace itself. You can allow it under System Settings › Privacy & Security › App Management, or replace it by hand.
upd.reasonDmg: The app is running from the disk image instead of from Applications.
upd.reasonLaunch: The installer could not be started automatically.
upd.reasonMinVersion: Your version is too old to update automatically.
upd.reasonPortable: This copy of souldew wasn’t installed with the installer (it runs from an unpacked folder), so it can’t update itself.
upd.reasonReadOnly: Your user account can’t write to the folder the app is in.
upd.reasonSignature: The new version’s signature could not be verified, so it was not installed automatically.
upd.reasonTranslocated: The app was opened straight from the download instead of from Applications.
upd.saveFirst: Save in the game first – restarting closes it.
upd.smartscreen: If Windows SmartScreen says it protected your PC, click “More info” › “Run anyway”. That is needed because souldew is not signed with a paid certificate.
upd.stepLaunch: Starting the installer – souldew closes and opens again by itself
